glosses: The act of abrading, wearing, or rubbing off; the wearing away by friction.

examples.text: The metal surface showed signs of abrasion after years of use.

glosses: The substance thus rubbed off; debris.

An abraded, scraped, or worn area.
A superficial wound caused by scraping; an area of skin where the cells on the surface have been scraped or worn away.

examples.text: The doctor cleaned the small skin abrasion on her knee.

glosses: The wearing away of the surface of the tooth by chewing.

glosses: To have on:

examples.text: He's wearing some nice pants today.
She wore her medals with pride.
Please wear your seatbelt.
Can you wear makeup and sunscreen at the same time?

glosses: To have on:
To have or carry on one's person habitually, consistently; or, to maintain in a particular fashion or manner.

examples.text: He wears eyeglasses.
She wears her hair in braids.

glosses: To have on:

examples.text: She wore a smile all day.

glosses: To erode:
To eat away at, erode, diminish, or consume gradually; to cause a gradual deterioration in; to produce (some change) through attrition, exposure, or constant use.

examples.text: You're going to wear a hole in the bottom of those shoes.
The water has slowly worn a channel into these rocks.
Long illness had worn the bloom from her cheeks.
Exile had worn the man to a shadow.

And They made the Moon, with his face wrinkled with many mountains and worn with a thousand valleys, to regard with pale eyes the games of the small gods, and to watch throughout the resting time of Māna-Yood-Sushāī; to watch, to regard all things, and be silent.

glosses: To erode:
To undergo gradual deterioration; become impaired; be reduced or consumed gradually due to any continued process, activity, or use.

examples.text: The tiles were wearing thin due to years of children's feet.
His stock of money[…] began to wear very low.
The family that had raised it wore out in the earlier part of this century

glosses: To erode:
To exhaust, fatigue, expend, or weary.

examples.text: His neverending criticism has finally worn my patience.

glosses: To erode:
(in the phrase \"wearing on (someone)\") To cause annoyance, irritation, fatigue, or weariness near the point of an exhaustion of patience.

examples.text: Her high pitched voice is really wearing on me lately.

glosses: To endure:
To overcome one's reluctance and endure a (previously specified) situation.

examples.text: I know you don't like working with him, but you'll just have to wear it.

glosses: To endure:

To last or remain durable under hard use or over time; to retain usefulness, value, or desirable qualities under any continued strain or long period of time; sometimes said of a person, regarding the quality of being easy or difficult to tolerate.

examples.text: Don't worry, this fabric will wear. These pants will last you for years.
This color wears so well. I must have washed this sweater a thousand times.
I have to say, our friendship has worn pretty well.
It's hard to get to know him, but he wears well.

glosses: To endure:
To pass slowly, gradually or tediously.

examples.text: wear on, wear away.
